analysis: Examined units: docs/architecture/inference.md head 4931-5378 (unchanged surrounding text; the only changes are line 3, the date, and line 2122, which documents per-request stop-string scope for Gemma 4 and <think> reasoning via ReasoningStopScope). Also examined the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump (7933a0f -> 7f00abc) and EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift. In EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift, head lines 15, 32, 64 and 159-160 thread an optional stopStringScope (default nil) through runPump and pump into matchedStopSequence. That value affects only usageSignal's matched-stop metadata. It does not change: encryption/terminal framing (T-008), KV/retirement release ordering, prefix-cache staging/receipt release (T-041 backstops at base 198-217, unchanged), billing usage via recordFinish, or cancellation. With a nil default, callers that pass no scope get the previous whole-output replay. Restricting the replay to the final message or non-reasoning spans reduces the chance of reporting a stop matched inside hidden reasoning, so there is no new exposure of reasoning text. The matched sequence is chosen from caller-supplied candidates. Remaining items not in evidence: matchedStopSequence in EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift, the callers of runPump that supply the scope, ReasoningStopScope, and the submodule diff contents. The submodule bump could change MLX inference/KV behaviour (TB-007, T-028, T-041), but its source is not supplied, so this is a coverage limit rather than a finding. No security regression identified.
